facts.did: go out to sea in a boat to fish; Eric asks about Vikemy's 'sacrifices' remark and Old Mother's readings; Ara hides her fortune from Eric to avoid worrying him

evidence.span:
“We need more readings from Old Mother. Something’s coming, I can feel it. What was Vikemy even talking about, anyway? People haven’t made sacrifices for us, have they?”


“He must mean Mother and Father,” I say, still rowing steadily. “When they…”

facts.did: sees a huge cylindrical gold smoking object (a hive ship) falling from the sky, spinning with flashing lights, plummeting toward the sea near them

evidence.span: A huge, cylindrical object, gold as a coin and smoking like a potion, is falling from the sky. Lights are flashing on it, and it’s spinning. It looks like a mechanical carousel. The kind that would be set up every year in the Palace grounds for the birthdays of the young princess.

facts.did: try to escape by rowing; Eric drops his net and shouts at Ara to row as the Temple bell rings and watchers swarm the beach

evidence.span:
Eric drops his net.


“Ara, row!” he shouts.


I grab the oars. My arms strain as I row. Everything feels as though it’s happening at twice the speed, like we’ve all caught fire.

facts.did: loses Eric in the fleeing crowd, is shoved, experiences a crushing episode (lead skull, head pain, white flashes), closes her eyes and loses time, finding herself last on the beach

evidence.span:
When I straighten up, I realise Eric is no longer by my side.


“Eric?” I scream, turning three hundred and sixty degrees. “Eric?” I can see a lot of fleeing people. But not my brother.

facts.did: hits the water with a crash and sinks; the impact creates a huge wave that smothers the beach and slams into the cliff; Ara jumps onto rocks to survive the wave

evidence.span:
I don’t have even a second to dwell on it, as at that moment the smoking ship hits the water. I watch in horror as the machine slips beneath the sea with a crash so loud the whole beach seems to sway.


Instantly, a huge wave leaps up from the impact and roars like an open mouth towards the shoreline.

facts.did: identifies the sinking ship's flag as royal blue (Rhavnan) and concludes Hevalla is winning the war

evidence.span:
The flag, I realise, is royal blue.


And my heart sinks faster than that ship. Because of course, of course, this is a Rhavnan ship. I’d hoped Vikemy had been exaggerating Hevalla’s successes in battle during Sermon. But this downed ship proves it. Despite its people having no blood magic, Hevalla is winning the war – or maybe has just won it.

facts.did: spots a body in Rhavnan blue in the water, swims out, pulls a Rhavnan soldier to shore, and performs chest compressions on him until he coughs up water and revives
facts.number_date: early twenties (soldier's apparent age); a thousand once mores (felt)

evidence.span:
I throw myself into the water. Swim harder, faster than I ever have. I don’t remember reaching him, only that I do. I pull the soldier towards me, lifting his head.


I can’t tell if he’s alive or dead.

facts.did: coughs up water, rises to his feet, searches himself, opens a rubber ball on his belt, takes out a gun and points it at Ara's head

evidence.span:
I watch as he finds a rubber ball connected with a cord to his belt, and prises it open with both hands.


A coldness creeps into my veins.


Because maybe I’ve made a mistake.


Maybe he hit his head in the fall or ingested too much water.


Maybe he’s not Rhavnan.


Maybe he is, but he’s a spy.


All I know is – and I know it now, in every fibre of my being – he’s dangerous.


I edge myself backwards. My heart is in my throat.


It’s too late.


The ball is open. And he’s pointing a gun at my head.
